about: Popular newsletters with their homepage and, where it can be justified, their official feed URL. Edit freely. An entry is verified: true only when a live `npm run verify:catalog` run (the "Catalog check" GitHub Actions workflow) showed its feed or public archive working, and verifiedAt (UTC date) and verifiedRunId record that run; everything else is verified: false. Discovery validates every feed live before storing it, so a wrong entry fails safely. feedUrl null means: discover from the homepage. archiveUrl (optional): the public archive page to read when no feed is found. pickerNote (optional): a short line the picker shows with the preview. unavailable (optional): Impartly cannot read this newsletter (refuses_automated_access: the site refuses automated readers), so the picker explains instead of fetching. note: for maintainers.

entries.name: TechCrunch
entries.note: Site-wide article feed (WordPress /feed/ convention); feed title TechCrunch, items are TechCrunch articles. TechCrunch's email newsletters do not have feeds of their own that we know of.

entries.name: StrictlyVC
entries.note: Unverified. Discovery finds https://strictlyvc.com/feed/ (feed title "StrictlyVC, LLC", daily issues named by date), but in the live check its first 3 items were issues titled with 2019 dates ("November 1, 2019" and earlier), so the feed looks stale and is not listed here. Discovery still reads the homepage; the picker preview shows the last issue date.

entries.name: Morning Brew
entries.note: Unverified. Discovery finds https://www.morningbrew.com/feed.xml, but the live check showed it carries site stories (/stories/..., e.g. shopping guides), not the daily newsletter issues, so it is not listed here. No public archive of the newsletter itself is known.

entries.name: Stratechery
entries.note: Public articles feed (WordPress /feed/ convention); feed title "Stratechery by Ben Thompson". Subscriber-only updates are not in it and are never fetched.

entries.name: Lenny's Newsletter
entries.note: Substack publication; Substack serves every publication's feed at /feed. Paid posts appear as previews and are marked partial.

entries.name: Not Boring
entries.note: Substack publication (/feed convention); items are the newsletter's posts (/p/...).

entries.name: Platformer
entries.note: Ghost publication (Ghost serves /rss/). Paid posts are marked partial.

entries.name: Exponential View
entries.note: Substack publication (/feed convention); items are the newsletter's posts (/p/...).

entries.name: The Pragmatic Engineer
entries.note: Substack publication (/feed convention). Many posts are paid and will be partial.

entries.name: Tomasz Tunguz
entries.note: Hugo site (Hugo serves /index.xml). The live check saw only 2 items in the feed.

entries.name: Benedict Evans
entries.pickerNote: These are Benedict Evans' essays, not the weekly newsletter, which is sent by email only.
entries.note: No feed (the live check got http_404 on the feed paths). archiveUrl is his essays page, read as a public archive: the live check listed 10 essays by <article> markup and read the newest (not partial). It holds the essays, not the weekly email newsletter, which has no public source we know of.

entries.name: The Generalist
entries.note: Feed found by discovery at /feed (Substack-style); the live check showed feed title "The Generalist", site link generalist.com and newsletter posts (/p/...), so it is the newsletter's own feed.

entries.name: Axios Pro Rata
entries.note: Kept so a search for it explains itself. Live checks (runs 45279821252, 45327358059 and 45333404039) got HTTP 403 on this page and no feed or archive, which Impartly does not work around.

entries.name: Term Sheet
entries.note: Unverified. Discovery finds a Fortune feed (https://fortune.com/feed/fortune-feeds/?id=3230629) from this page, but the live check showed feed title "Fortune FORTUNE" and general Fortune articles, not Term Sheet issues, so it is not listed here. May be partly paywalled; anything behind it is not read.
